item.title: Group outlines spending plan for new climate change tax
item.description: The new Green Fee Advisory Council had to choose from among more than $2 billion worth of funding requests to help Hawaii respond to climate change, but will only have $100 million or so annually to recommend through the first statewide tax of its kind in the country, which has been collecting revenue since Jan. 1.

item.title: EDITORIAL: Anti-nepotism bills lift up government
item.description: Government corruption, or at least misconduct on a significant or widespread scale, seems relatively uncommon in the islands. Cases of bribery or graft, for example, are typically few and far between, and when such dealings do come to light, they are met with appropriate shock and disdain. That is a good thing; political misdeeds certainly have no place in a state so heavily dependent on government leadership and whose representatives boast uniquely close ties to the community.

item.title: Waimea girls, Kauai boys strong at latest Kauai Interscholastic Federation Wrestling
item.description: Waimea High School wrestling program turned the girls’ leaderboard blue with Menehune honors on Saturday during the Kauai Interscholastic Federation wrestling matches held at the Bernice Hundley Gym.

item.title: Kauai kane paddlers are Div. II No. 2
item.description: HONOLULU — The Kauai High School varsity boys outrigger canoe paddling team had a strong showing during the 2026 Hawaiian Airlines Hawaii High School Athletic Association Canoe Paddling State Championships that ran under threatening weather conditions on Saturday at Keehi Lagoon on Oahu.

item.title: New CPR machines coming to Wilcox
item.description: HONOLULU — A new cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) machine is scheduled to appear at the Wilcox Medical Center thanks to the generosity of a charitable trust.

item.title: ‘Hearts and Horses’ weekend full of activity
item.description: LIHUE — A lively weekend of excitement including Chinese lions, firecrackers and a variety of music and dancing awaits Kauai residents from Friday and continuing through the weekend at different places from around the island.

item.title: Hawaii Lt. Gov. Sylvia Luke faces more scrutiny
item.description: The Hawaii Campaign Spending Commission will investigate whether Lt. Gov. Sylvia Luke violated state law when she failed to report $16,000 in campaign contributions, including $10,000 tied to a businessman involved in a high-profile bankruptcy.

item.title: Tighter laws, tougher penalties sought by lawmakers
item.description: More bills aimed at “clean government” have been introduced again this legislative session ahead of the November general elections that will determine the future of all 51 House seats and 13 of the 25 Senate seats amid an ongoing Attorney General’s investigation into the identity of a mystery legislator who allegedly accepted $35,000 “in funds.”
